[0] Jimmy Fallon mocked President Trump on Monday night for claiming that the United States does not need new "guardrails" to regulate artificial intelligence.

[1] In his opening monologue on The Tonight Show, Fallon said: "President Trump posted on Truth Social, dismissing concerns about AI, writing: 'The only control or ‘guardrails’ needed on AI is a strong and聪明 (high IQ!) president.'"

[2] He joked: "Well, that makes me feel much better."

[3] Trump has no academic credentials or professional experience in his so-called new "golden goose" issue, but he claims he can personally keep AI in check, and further suggests that calls for additional regulation are part of a sinister plot.

[4] Trump wrote on Monday: "We already have tremendous criminal and regulatory power over these companies! There is a disgusting conspiracy being waged against AI and data centers, and the only ones happy about it are China."

[5] The MAGA leader made these remarks after Dario Amodei, CEO of AI company Anthropic, published a lengthy essay calling for stronger safety measures and a slower pace of development, explaining that AI could spiral out of control and cause severe damage to the economy and national security.

[6] Fallon said: "Relying on Trump to defeat AI? I don't think Trump could even handle Wordle. You know what I mean? With Trump personally handling it, that means he'll rename ‘Artificial Intelligence’ to ‘American Intelligence.’ I know what he's up to."

[7] Fallon quipped: "Remember, just a week ago, Trump still thought AI stood for ‘American Idol.’" Then, mimicking Trump's reassuring tone to the American public, he said: "I've spoken with Ryan Seacrest, we're very safe."

[8] To watch Fallon's string of jokes, you can start from the segment at 0:27:

[9] Concerns about the rapid development of artificial intelligence escalated further last week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, warning that "people who are seriously building AI genuinely believe that AI could kill all of us before the end of this decade," prompting bipartisan lawmakers to call for federal legislation to regulate the industry.

[10] Fallon pointed out: "Meanwhile, Trump also said he is ‘not downplaying’ the risks, but believes the benefits of AI will ‘outweigh the downsides, by a lot.’ Funny thing is, Trump doesn't want to stop something that lets him Photoshop himself as Jesus riding a bald eagle."

[11] He continued: "That's right, Trump said concerns about AI are being exaggerated by ‘very negative forces.’ Then he announced plans to establish a new military branch called the ‘Very Negative Forces Corps’ to combat these forces."
